classification: operator error against documented behaviour, not a code defect
corrective_action: every D5 shell invocation passes COGOS_POSTGRES_ENV_FILE=$PWD/.env.s21d5.local. The D5 databases were then migrated correctly and cognitive_os_s21d5_test reports alembic head 0015, 114 cognitive_os tables, and 'No new upgrade operations detected' from alembic check.

damage.migration_kind: additive; both create tables and neither drops or rewrites one

not_rolled_back: deliberate. cognitive_os_dev is the development database, holds no evidence for any sprint, and was stale at 0013 against a repository head of 0015. The two applied migrations are additive and their tables are empty. A downgrade would be a second unintended write, executing DROP statements against a database that is now simply current. The state is recorded rather than reversed.
subject: the D5 migration was first applied to the development database
superseded_reading: the first migration-check failure of this wave reported a TEXT versus Numeric(5,4) drift on cognitive_os.experience_step_assessments.confidence. That drift belongs to cognitive_os_dev alone. cognitive_os_s21d4_test and cognitive_os_s21d5_test both report numeric(5,4), which is what the model declares, so neither the D4 release nor the D5 provisioning carries the drift.
what_a_reader_should_take_from_it: the loader's stated purpose is to stop a mis-scoped command reaching a real database. In this instance it redirected a mis-scoped command into a different real database instead, silently. That is an observation about the fallback target, not a request to change a deliberate design; the release owner decides whether a mis-scoped invocation should be refused rather than redirected.
what_happened: S21D5-001 invoked scripts/postgres_migrate.sh and scripts/postgres_migration_check.sh with the D5 environment exported into the shell (set -a; . ./.env.s21d5.local; set +a). scripts/postgres_common.sh re-reads .env.postgres.local under set -a and overrides exported values, so both commands targeted cognitive_os_dev rather than cognitive_os_s21d5_test. The development database was upgraded from alembic 0013 to 0015.
why_not_a_defect: docs/operations/learned-evidence.md lines 238 to 240 state the override explicitly and call it deliberate: 'Exporting the variables directly is not enough - the shared loader re-reads its own file and will override them, which is deliberate: it is what stops a mis-scoped command reaching a real database.' The released convention is COGOS_POSTGRES_ENV_FILE=$PWD/.env.<sprint>.local and every released operations document uses it. The loader behaved as designed and as documented; the invocation did not follow the document.
